text.p: Greg Norman said on Tuesday he was concerned about security for players at golf tournaments and was having discussions with other golfers on ways to improve the situation.
"A couple of times I have feared for my safety," the Australian said, refusing to specify when or where. But he said that he and other players had made suggestions to officials to tighten security.

"We are aware of what has happened and what can happen and we are having a bit of a think-tank on it," said Norman, who is in Scotland to play in the Loch Lomond World Invitational starting on Wednesday and the British Open at Royal Troon next week.

"People nowadays feel they know the athletes better because the media exposure is better. People feel because they see you all the time they know you and they feel like they can say something whether they like you or dislike you.
"It happens to me and to everybody. I've seen the change over the last couple of years."
He said the availability of alcohol at courses had contributed to the problem. "Maybe it should be like baseball, where they close the bar at 3 pm," he said.
"There have been more younger people coming out to watch and Tiger (Woods) has had a big effect on that," added Norman, who won the St Jude Classic in Memphis 10 days ago.
"So therefore you get people who don't really understand what golf is all about."
Norman said the game was healthier now than it had ever been.
"I haven't ever seen the game of golf as strong and as healthy as it is right now," he said.
"Wall Street is in love with the game of golf. There are more people from Wall Street playing golf than ever. And Wall Street is the heartbeat of America.
"From the business point of view, from the player point of view, I think we are just so lucky to be here right now for the next four or five years, or as long as it lasts.
"It happened before Tiger came out on the scene. There is something about it. You have a major corporation (aircraft makers Gulfstream) sponsoring golf here in Scotland. What does that tell you?"
He said the coming of Woods, who replaced him as world number one by winning the Western Open on Sunday, had helped accelerate the sport's popularity.

"Anybody with the charisma he has got would obviously accelerate it. Let's be honest, we were all hoping someone new would come along. You guys were tired of interviewing us all the time. You needed a new story. It was pretty much the same group of guys the past 10 or 15 years.
"We all needed someone new. And it's Tiger Woods. And it's good for the game of golf."
South African Ernie Els, who won the U.S. Open last month, shared some of Norman's views on player safety though he said that he had not personally felt endangered.
"There should be a little more control," Els said. "In America it is a bit of a hassle and at the U.S. Open it was on the edge of being out of control."
